---
title: "Gatekeeper (Initial Filtering)"
---

The “Gatekeeper” task has several subtasks:

- Filter reads using fastp
- Detect which species have reads within the input FASTQ files (Kraken 2 <https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-019-1891-0>)
- Identify the subset of reads in the taxon of interest (Myco pipeline only. Used to select mycobacteriaceae from Kraken 2 results)

# Thresholds

## Fastp

There are several options used for the filtering with fastp, explained here [gatekeeper\_pipeline/README.md at main · GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/gatekeeper\_pipeline (github.com)](https://github.com/GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/gatekeeper_pipeline/blob/main/README.md#fastp-default-parameters). Main one to note is that reads with length less than 50 (100 for ONT) are removed.

## kraken2

Within the myco option for gatekeeper, a threshold of 10,000 Mycobacteriaceae reads (or 1000 for ONT) is used. Only samples with equal or greater number of reads classed as Mycobacteriaceae proceed to the rest of the pipeline.


# Detection of species

Kraken 2 maps *k*-mers from FASTQ reads against a hash table of *k*-mers of known taxonomic classification, resulting in a table showing assignments of fragments to taxa. It will then assign each read to a taxa individually based on the *k*-mers. Generally it will take the most common taxa, but should use the Lowest Common Ancestor in cases like ties between species in same genus. Unsure of exact rules here.

*Extract from example Kraken 2 output (cloumn definitions: *<https://github.com/DerrickWood/kraken2/blob/master/docs/MANUAL.markdown#sample-report-output-format>*)*


### Performance

Kraken2 is used widely and does seem to be the best performing, but highly dependent of databases, parameters and use of bracken.

- [Benchmarking taxonomic classifiers with Illumina and Nanopore sequence data for clinical metagenomic diagnostic applications | Microbiology Society (microbiologyresearch.org)](https://www.microbiologyresearch.org/content/journal/mgen/10.1099/mgen.0.000886)
- Paper comparing parameters within Kraken2: [From defaults to databases: parameter and database choice dramatically impact the performance of metagenomic taxonomic classification tools | Microbiology Society (microbiologyresearch.org)](https://www.microbiologyresearch.org/content/journal/mgen/10.1099/mgen.0.000949?crawler=true)
- Another comparing parameters with simulated data, includes standard database. But does not consider bracken: [Impact of database choice and confidence score on the performance of taxonomic classification using Kraken2 | aBIOTECH (springer.com)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42994-024-00178-0)

### Confidence Scoring (currently not used for production)

Kraken2 assigns each read to a taxa independently. The confidence score can be used to require that a read had a sufficiently good match by requiring `x%` of k-mers to be assigned to the taxa label (or a descendent) to actually assign the read. If not it will continue up the taxa hierarchy until it reaches the required threshold. Settings described in full [here](https://github.com/DerrickWood/kraken2/blob/master/docs/MANUAL.markdown#confidence-scoring).

Currently we use the default cut-off which is 0. Recommendations online range drastically. The best comparison I (Matthew) found was a paper comparing Kraken2 and MetPhlAn 3 along with various databases and settings ([paper](https://www.microbiologyresearch.org/content/journal/mgen/10.1099/mgen.0.000949?crawler=true)). They don’t give any hard rules. But for the standard database we use and preference for recall (instead of precision) it looks like 0.1 to 0.15 would be best.

There is also some discussion on a github thread [here](https://github.com/DerrickWood/kraken2/issues/265)

### Distinct Minimizers

Kraken2 can report the number of **distinct k-mers** associated with each taxa from the input reads. This is an experimental feature, but could be helpful. In the kraken2 output report it add a column telling you the total number of distinct minimizers (compact k-mer representation) used. This could tell you that all hits for species X only came from a small number of minimizers and so might be dubious. Details [here](https://github.com/DerrickWood/kraken2/blob/master/docs/MANUAL.markdown#distinct-minimizer-count-information)

Current experiments suggest this would be difficult to use automatically.
